description: A modern, high-performance local file search and productivity tool for Windows. A sleek, customizable alternative to Everything and Listary built with C# WPF and NT Services, featuring instant NTFS MFT parsing, real-time USN monitoring, and plugin support.
post_install: Write-Host "lertaro: migrating the previous installation ($(Split-Path $previous -Leaf)) into this version."

$extras = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $previous -Force -ErrorAction Ignore | Where-Object { $reserved -notcontains $_.Name } | ForEach-Object { if ($_.PSIsContainer) { Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction Ignore } else { $_ } } | Where-Object { $relative = $_.FullName.Substring($previous.Length + 1); (($_.Attributes -band [System.IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) -eq 0) -and !(Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $target $relative) -PathType Leaf) })

foreach ($file in $extras) { $destination = Join-Path $stage $file.FullName.Substring($previous.Length + 1); New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path $destination) | Out-Null; Copy-Item -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Destination $destination -Force }
# An elevated PowerShell must not discover modules from a user's custom module search path, and
# every tool is called by full path from System32: PATH is the user's to change, and a matching
# name in it would run at administrator integrity.
# The service owns the index files in Data while it runs, and the folder is locked down against
# ordinary rights, so everything below has to happen elevated.
# A minute, not less: the service writes its index out on the way down, and on a machine in
# the middle of a full rebuild that is the difference between a migration and a torn copy.
if (!$stopped) { $summary.Errors += 'LertaroService did not stop within a minute; the data was left untouched.' }
# The updater stops, replaces and restarts the service itself, and reports through
# update-result.json, which the caller reads back.
} else { $summary.Errors += 'portable-updater.ps1 is missing from the new version; the staged files were not applied.' }

try { if ($elevated) { Start-Process -FilePath $powerShell -ArgumentList $arguments -Wait -NoNewWindow -ErrorAction Stop } else { Start-Process -FilePath $powerShell -ArgumentList $arguments -Verb RunAs -Wait -ErrorAction Stop } } catch { Write-Host "lertaro: the migration needs administrator approval and was skipped: $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Yellow }
if ($summary.Data -gt 7) { Write-Host 'lertaro: part of the data could not be copied.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }
} else { Write-Host 'lertaro: the migration did not run, the previous data was left untouched.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }

if ($stage -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $target 'update-result.json'))) { $result = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $target 'update-result.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json; if ($result.Status -ne 'success') { Write-Host "lertaro: the updater reported: $($result.Message)" -ForegroundColor Yellow } }

if ($stage -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $stage)) { try { [System.IO.Directory]::Delete($stage, $true) } catch { Write-Host "lertaro: the staging folder $stage could not be removed." -ForegroundColor Yellow } }
} else { Write-Host 'lertaro: no previous installation to migrate.' }
pre_uninstall: # The service runs as LocalSystem from this folder, and the installation locked the folder down to
# SYSTEM and Administrators, so everything below has to happen elevated.

if (((@(& $sc query LertaroService 2>$null)) -join ' ') -match '1060') { $summary.Service = 'removed' } else { $summary.Service = 'failed'; $summary.Errors += 'LertaroService could not be removed; it may still be stopping.' }

Get-Process -Name $name -ErrorAction Ignore | Where-Object { $path = $null; try { $path = $_.Path } catch { }; $path -and $path.StartsWith($Target + '\', [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) } | ForEach-Object { try { $_.Kill(); $_.WaitForExit(15000) | Out-Null } catch { } }
# Hand the folder back to Administrators and the uninstalling user so Scoop can delete it: the
# service's Data folders are owned by other accounts' SIDs and refuse ordinary rights.

try { if ($elevated) { Start-Process -FilePath $powerShell -ArgumentList $arguments -Wait -NoNewWindow -ErrorAction Stop } else { Start-Process -FilePath $powerShell -ArgumentList $arguments -Verb RunAs -Wait -ErrorAction Stop } } catch { Write-Host "lertaro: the cleanup needs administrator approval and was skipped: $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Yellow }
} else { Write-Host 'lertaro: the elevated cleanup did not run; the service and the folder permissions were left untouched, and Scoop may fail to delete the folder.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }
